source.title: Analyzing & Eliminating Learning Rate Warmup in GPT Pre-Training
source.authors: Atli Kosson; Bettina Messmer; Martin Jaggi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether controlling different update-size measures removes the warmup-related performance gap in GPT pre-training, and finds that weight-space controls reduce but do not eliminate it; representation-change control removes the benefit in the tested setup. It also reports a CIFAR-10 intervention on large early updates and related performance effects.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the study's reported warmup comparisons, optimizer modifications, representation-change correction, and controlled early-update experiments. Cited results from prior work are not included. Figure-only GPT sweep outcomes are recorded as figure only because exact values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study tests warmup and early-update interventions, not any listed claim version. GPT experiments hold batch size at 480; the batch-size analysis predicts representation changes rather than measuring held-out performance across batch sizes. Neither optimizer comparisons nor CIFAR-10 early-learning-rate interventions test V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Parameter-space update control generally does not reproduce warmup's benefits; relative representation change is promising, and high momentum combined with angular-update control and inverse bias correction may enable warmup-free training. These results require validation beyond the single main GPT2 configuration.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates learning-rate warmup and optimizer/update-size modifications in GPT pre-training, plus controlled large early updates in a CIFAR-10 ResNet-20. The original claim versions concern memorization and generalization conditions or measurements; this study does not test those protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Warmup percentage and learning rate; optimizer and update-size control (AdamW, LionA, LionAR, RRC correction); momentum and its scheme; large initial learning-rate factor; activation function; bias freezing; training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Warmup improves GPT2 validation loss at batch size 480. Controlling update norms or angular updates leaves a warmup advantage; an SNR-based representation-change correction removes it with slightly worse overall performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warmup benefits in this GPT2 setting depend on early-update properties that parameter-space update size alone does not capture.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing momentum degrades GPT2 performance. With higher momentum, Nesterov momentum, and inverse bias correction, no-warmup LionAR performs best; LionA still benefits from warmup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum and angular-update control jointly affect whether explicit warmup improves GPT2 training.

fits_no_version.finding: Enlarged early updates lower standard ResNet-20 CIFAR-10 accuracy, with degradation persisting under longer training. Leaky ReLU reduces the degradation, and freezing biases mitigates it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large early updates can cause lasting accuracy losses whose severity depends on activation functions and bias training.

record.peer_reviewed: HiLD 2024: 2nd Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: Main experiments focus on a single GPT2 network. Many GPT sweep results are figure-only and do not provide exact values in the text. Uncertainty is not quantified for every GPT configuration. The CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 experiments are described as controlled experiments conducted due to resource constraints; the authors state that their promising approaches need validation across additional settings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were omitted. Measurements such as gradient SNR, ℓ2-update size, angular updates, relative representation change, dead ReLU rates, and stable rank are mentioned as candidate explanatory properties; the text's figure panels do not give extractable numerical values for these measurements, and they are not measures of the claim versions. Figure 6's exact accuracy points across epoch counts are not stated in prose and are not extracted separately; the text states qualitatively that longer training did not recover standard ReLU performance.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; switching optimizers or isolating decoupled weight decay.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, including whether recipe adaptations remove a measured batch-size penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including interactions with training-set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly link to none. Their states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, without disputing the reported warmup and early-update findings. Citations to original sources and discussion of critical batch size do not establish a test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence were not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking was measured.
